text:
Utah plays like one of the better teams in the West, and its goaltending keeps hiding it. The Mammoth have 54.8% of the expected goals (the quality of chances on both sides), 57% at five on five, and create 3.41 expected goals an hour. By chances they should have about 34 points. They have 31, sitting 14-10-3 with a 72% playoff chance by our simulations, and the gap is in net: Utah has allowed about 14 more goals than its chances against predicted.

Friday's 6-5 shootout win in Nashville was all of it at once. The Mammoth out-attempted the Predators 78-48 and built 4.01 expected goals to 2.26, and Karel Vejmelka still allowed five on 21 shots. Whether Sebastian Cossa is ready to be the No. 1 is a live question in Utah's own coverage. Either way, a team this good at controlling play doesn't need great goaltending, only ordinary goaltending.

The lineup is deep. Anders Lee, Kailer Yamamoto and Barrett Hayton have 74% of the expected goals together, and Lee scored twice Friday, including the tying goal with four minutes left. Logan Cooley and Vincent Trocheck have driven a second group; MacKenzie Weegar and Mikhail Sergachev are the top pair at 56%. Two days ago they ended Minnesota's 15-game point streak. Watch the crease.
